thread:
Taylor: Opening a quick thread: we prototyped a lightweight 'splitter' microservice to emit provisional token deltas during generation. goal: zero-penalty on latency path and still produce auditable deltas for billing.
Sam: Nice. How are you making sure provisional deltas don't create charge duplication when retries or client-side reconnects happen?
Taylor: We use a deterministic key: (tenant_id, request_id, generation_idx). Splitter uses that as the Kafka key so duplicates collapse. Also provisional messages contain a small fingerprint of the prompt + model to help finalizer decide idempotency.
Rina: What about long-running streaming sessions where the same generation_id evolves as user continues typing? Do we roll provisional entries or emit incremental ones?
Taylor: We emit incremental provisional deltas grouped by flush windows. Default flush: 150 tokens or 2s. For streaming with function-calls we lower to 50 tokens. Grouping helps keep event volume down.
Omar: Buffering raises crash-loss concerns. If the host dies before flushing, we'll miss provisional entries. Can finalizer detect and reconcile once full ledger entry arrives later?
Taylor: Yes. Finalizer performs an atomic merge by generation_idx. If the ledger already contains matching tokens, it marks provisional as reconciled and drops duplicate credits. If not, the finalizer will create the canonical entry and emit a reconciled marker.
Sam: Auditors will ask for the exact prompt/model combo that generated tokens. Where do you store that proof data?
Taylor: Proof-frames live in the audit store (immutable blob store). Provisional events include a proof_ref (s3 uri) plus a small inline fingerprint. Proof-frames are compact JSON (prompt_hash, model_id, sequence_metadata).
Rina: Multi-tenant fairness: batching can delay visibility of charges for high-QPS small requests. We should add tenant-specific flush thresholds and an emergency flush triggered by quota-check requests.
Omar: Good call. Also we should make provisional-marked deltas visible to quota service with soft quotas. Only final ledger entries enforce hard quota. That avoids blocking user requests on reconciliation.
Sam: Implementation detail: topic layout? I suggest splitter.provisional (compacted by key), canonical.billing (append-only), and a repair topic orphan.provisional for TTL-evicted entries. Repair worker picks those up and tries to reconcile.
Taylor: Exactly. TTL is short (4m) to avoid long partials; repair worker gets checkpointed offsets and exposes metrics: orphan_rate, reconcile_lag, emit_latency.
Rina: Edge-case: partial KV-cache hits mid-generation may shift attribution between cache and model. Example: first N tokens from cache, rest generated. How do we reflect that without double-counting?
Taylor: We tag provisional deltas with origin="cache" or "model" per token-span. Finalizer merges spans deterministically and dedupes overlaps using token indexes. We also include a contiguous token-range in the proof-frame.
Omar: Security/privileges: proof-frames contain prompt hashes only, not plaintext prompts, to avoid leakage. Support can request plaintext via controlled audit flow.
billing-bot: canary update: splitter v0.2 rolled to staging. metrics: provisional_emits=350/s, p95 emit_latency=8ms, orphan_rate=0.6%.
Taylor: Next steps: write RFC with sequence diagrams for happy path + crash + partition + duplicate generation_id. Add recommended SLOs: emit_latency < 20ms p99, reconciliation < 120s for 99.9%, orphan_rate < 0.1% after repair optimizations.
Sam: I'll own infra checklist (retention, topic compaction, repair scaling).
Rina: I'll prototype tenant-aware flush policies and run a bursty tenant sim.
Omar: I'll draft the proof-frame schema (fingerprints, token ranges, model meta) and suggest RBAC for audit reads.
Taylor: thanks all. I'll open the RFC draft and ping eng-platform for review. :rocket:
